definitions.gloss: running for office; standing as a candidate
definitions.explanation: Entering a political election as a candidate. The most common modern use of this word.

definitions.gloss: entering a competition; stepping into the fray
definitions.explanation: More broadly, stepping forward to take on a challenge or competition. Originally referred to riding out to battle on horseback.

examples.japanese: {市長|しちょう}{選挙|せんきょ}に{出馬|しゅつば}する。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{来年|らいねん}の{国政|こくせい}{選挙|せんきょ}への{出馬|しゅつば}を{表明|ひょうめい}した。
examples.english: She announced her candidacy for next year's national election.

examples.japanese: {現職|げんしょく}の{知事|ちじ}が{三選|さんせん}を{目指|めざ}して{出馬|しゅつば}した。
examples.english: The incumbent governor ran for a third term.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}{自|みずか}ら{出馬|しゅつば}して{交渉|こうしょう}にあたった。
examples.english: The president himself stepped in to handle the negotiations.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}のプロジェクトには{部長|ぶちょう}が{出馬|しゅつば}することになった。
examples.english: The department head will be stepping in for this project.

examples.japanese: ベテラン{選手|せんしゅ}が{代表|だいひょう}{戦|せん}に{出馬|しゅつば}する{可能性|かのうせい}がある。
examples.english: There is a possibility that the veteran player will enter the national team match.

notes:
Literally "riding out on horseback" ({出|しゅつ} = go out + {馬|ば} = horse). Originally a military term for riding into battle, now primarily used for political candidacy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {選挙|せんきょ}に{出馬|しゅつば}する (to run in an election)
- {出馬|しゅつば}を{表明|ひょうめい}する (to announce one's candidacy)
- {出馬|しゅつば}を{見送|みおく}る (to decide not to run)
- {出馬|しゅつば}{要請|ようせい} (request to run for office)

USAGE:
In political contexts, {出馬|しゅつば} is the standard word for announcing or entering a candidacy. The extended sense (a senior person personally stepping in) carries a nuance of someone important entering the scene to take charge.
